SnowRaven · Design refinement

The raven lands in the mark

One mark, every surface: the new serif SR, with the raven's head worked into the S, replaces the old monogram on the Dock, the taskbar, the home screen, and the browser tab. The brand green (#2D8653) carries straight through, so it reads as SnowRaven grown up, not a different app.

Today (v0.5.92)
→
The new mark

macOS Dock — one decision to make

Your .icns draws the tile edge-to-edge, exactly as the app does today. Native macOS apps draw inside Apple's icon grid (the tile at ~82% of the canvas), so a full-canvas icon reads slightly oversized next to them. Both shown against the same neighbors:

A · Full canvas

The tile fills the slot, as v0.5.92 does. Bolder, but sits a touch large in the row.

Recommended

B · Apple icon grid

The tile drawn at 82% with a transparent margin — the size every native app sits at.

iOS home screen

iOS masks the icon itself, so it ships as the full-bleed square on the brand green — already saved with no alpha channel, which is exactly what the App Store check demands. All 36 committed PNGs get rebuilt from it.

Windows taskbar

Your .ico already carries all seven sizes (16 through 256) and Windows shows icons unmasked, so it ships as provided — square corners are the platform's own look. The installer and Start tile use the same file.

Browser tab — the web app's icon

Today's favicon is a different bird entirely (a line-drawn glyph that never matched the desktop icon). The refresh unifies it: a new favicon built from the traced vector master, same rounded green tile.

SnowRaven — today's tab
SnowRaven — refreshed
eBird

Small sizes — does the raven survive?

The serif SR stays legible all the way down; the raven's head reads clearly at 48px and above, and at 16–24px it gracefully becomes texture inside the S rather than noise. No small-size simplification needed.

The one scope question: the website

The public site's header mark and its own favicon are the same old line-drawn bird. Updating them is outside the app bundle (no version bump of its own, ships with the Pages deploy) — but leaving them makes the site disagree with every screenshot of the new icon. I recommend bringing both along:
